zh: 回文由前一半（长度 ⌊n/2⌋）和可能存在的中心字符唯一确定，后一半就是前一半的反转。输入本身是回文，所以至多一个字母出现奇数次；n 为奇数时它只能放在中心。
比较两个回文的字典序时，最先比较的就是前一半。前一半的字符多重集是固定的（每个字母取出现次数的一半），多重集固定时，非降序排列的字典序最小。
统计 26 个字母的出现次数，然后按 a 到 z 的顺序，把每个字母的 ⌊cnt/2⌋ 个副本同时从左端和右端往中间填，奇数次字母放在下标 n/2 处。长度可达三千万，整块读入、一次写出，额外空间只有输出串本身。
en: A palindrome is determined by its first half (length ⌊n/2⌋) and a possible center character; the second half is the reverse of the first. The input is itself a palindrome, so at most one letter occurs an odd number of times; when n is odd, that letter can only go in the center.

When comparing two palindromes lexicographically, the first half is what gets compared first. The multiset of characters in the first half is fixed (half the count of each letter), and for a fixed multiset the non-decreasing arrangement is lexicographically smallest.

Count the 26 letters, then in order from a to z place ⌊cnt/2⌋ copies of each letter at the left end and the right end at the same time, moving toward the middle, and put the odd-count letter at index n/2. The length can reach thirty million, so read in bulk and write once; the only extra space is the output string itself.

explanationEn:
## Problem

You are given a string letters made of lowercase letters that is itself a palindrome. Rearrange its characters and, among all arrangements that are still palindromes, output the lexicographically smallest one.

## Derivation

A palindrome is uniquely determined by its first half (length ⌊n/2⌋) and a possible center character; the second half is the reverse of the first half. The input itself is a palindrome, so at most one letter has an odd count: when n is odd, exactly one letter occurs an odd number of times and it can only go in the center; when n is even there is no center.

When two palindromes are compared lexicographically, the first half is exactly what is compared first. The multiset of characters of the first half is fixed as "half the count of each letter", and among all arrangements of a fixed multiset, the non-decreasing order is lexicographically smallest. The center character is already uniquely determined, so the answer is: the first half in non-decreasing order from a to z, the odd-count letter (if any) in the middle, followed by the reverse of the first half.

## Correctness

In any palindromic arrangement, position i and position n−1−i hold the same character, so each letter appears exactly ⌊cnt/2⌋ times in the first half, and the center (if any) can only be the unique odd-count letter. So the palindromic arrangements correspond one to one with "an arrangement of the first half". Among them, the smaller the first half lexicographically, the smaller the whole string, and the smallest arrangement of a multiset is the non-decreasing order. The constructed string really is a palindrome and has the same character multiset as the input, so it is the answer.

## Complexity

Counting the 26 letters is O(n), filling from both ends toward the middle is O(n), and the extra space is the output string itself. The length can reach thirty million, so the reference reads everything in blocks with fread and outputs with a single fwrite.

## Independent verification

The oracle sorts the input, removes the center character, and takes every other character to get the first half, without reusing count-based filling; for large cases it also checks item by item that the output is a palindrome, that its letter counts equal the input's, and that the first half is non-decreasing. Small-domain exhaustive check: every palindrome of length 1..7 over the alphabet {a,b,c}; for each input, all distinct arrangements are enumerated, palindromes are filtered and the smallest taken, and the reference program is actually run on each. Four wrong programs that exit normally (just sorting, echoing the input, taking the lexicographically largest, putting the odd-count letter first) are each judged wrong on the formal cases.
